subject: Call recap: Long-document workflows & evaluation next steps
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@clariontx.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Call recap: Long-document workflows & evaluation next steps

Hi Aisha — great to meet earlier. Thanks for walking us through the Clarion use case (clinical protocol ingestion + long-form summarization for reviewers). Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

Key takeaways from the call:
- Required window: many source documents >150k tokens; canonical workflows involve multi-doc aggregation and iterative summarization.
- Primary outputs: concise reviewer summaries (2–3 paragraphs) + structured QA (entity extraction + compliance flags).
- SLO: median latency target ~3s for interactive review slices; nightly batch for full archive processing acceptable.
- Compliance: data residency + audit trail — Clarion needs exportable logs and per-model usage records.

Our recommended initial evaluation plan (short):
1) Pilot with 3 models across two modes: a) high-fidelity long-window model (redwood/cascade-70b-32k) b) cost-optimized long-window quantized variant (redwood/cascade-70b-32k-q4) c) efficient long-form model for segmentation (redwood/longform-lite-30b-64k).
2) Run a 500-document benchmark (samples you shared + synthetic edge cases). Metrics: summarization ROUGE-L, BERTScore, extractive recall for compliance entities, and truncation error rate (percent of docs where important context was lost).
3) Prompt sets: we will run 3 strategies — sliding-window lead-in + hierarchical summarize, chunk-and-stitch with refactoring prompts, and prefix-KV caching with incremental aggregation.

Attachments we’ll deliver: long_window_benchmarks_v3.csv (summary of our pre-run), prompt_set_clarion_v1.json (starter prompts & eval harness), mutual_action_plan_clarion.docx (timeline & scope).

Immediate asks from you:
- Confirm the 500-sample set (we used the documents you uploaded to the shared Drive) or send any additional protected examples to the secure upload URL.
- Legal/Compliance point-of-contact for SOC2 + data retention questions (we'll loop in private deployment options if needed).

Next steps I propose:
- Dev will send the technical runbook and benchmark links tomorrow (Dev: see thread).
- If the metrics look good, Marissa will propose pilot pricing and timeline (2–4 weeks).

Thanks again — I’ll check in after Dev’s bench notes.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Call recap: Long-document workflows & evaluation next steps

Rishi / Aisha — adding the technical notes and the initial benchmark summary. Attaching: long_window_benchmarks_v3.csv and prompt_set_clarion_v1.json.

Short technical summary of what we observed in the test run (500 documents, mixed real + synthetic):
- Truncation behavior: vanilla short-window models truncated critical protocol sections >16k tokens. The cascade-70b-32k maintains context for most single-doc cases up to ~30k tokens before quality drops; above ~32k we see ordering degradation for extractive tasks.
- Summarization fidelity: hierarchical summarize (chunk -> compress -> synthesize) outperformed single-pass long answer in ROUGE-L (~+6 points) and in entity recall (~+8%).
- KV/prefix caching: enabling KV cache + incremental prefix passing reduced repeated compute on overlapping context windows by ~35% and improved latency for interactive slices.
- Failure modes: 1) Important tables encoded as inline text lost structure in chunk boundaries; 2) Latency spikes when sequence lengths cross an internal tiling boundary (we can mitigate with model routing).

Model recommendations (practical):
- Phase 1 (pilot): ran cascade-70b-32k as baseline for fidelity and longform-lite-30b-64k for a cost/throughput comparison. Use q4 quant for nightly batch (cost savings ~45%).
- Inference config: continuous batching disabled for interactive review routes; enable small-window batching and prefix caching for reviewer session endpoints. Set max_output_tokens conservative (512) for summaries.

Proposed eval metrics & thresholds (we'll compute these in the Drive sheet):
- Summarization ROUGE-L >= 0.42 vs human summary baseline
- Extractive recall for compliance entities >= 0.88
- Truncation error rate <= 5% (documents where required context is missing from final summary)
- Median interactive slice latency <= 3s at p50 with reserved capacity

Links:
- Benchmark file: https://drive.redwood.ai/teams/eval/clarion/benchmarks_v3.xlsx
- Eval harness (internal): https://git.redwood.ai/clarion/long-window-harness (will grant access to Clarion devs if needed)

I’ll run an additional targeted pass on the table/appendix handling (structured extraction) and push a prompt variant that preserves table delimiters.

—Dev
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Call recap: Long-document workflows & evaluation next steps

Thanks — helpful notes. A few clarifying Qs from our side before we commit samples: 

1) Summarization fidelity — when you say hierarchical summarize did better, can you share an example where the single-pass model dropped an entity or changed clinical meaning? We need a reproducible failure case to show our reviewers.

2) Truncation error rate — how do you compute "required context"? For us, the required context may be a protocol section referenced many pages earlier. Can the eval harness flag these as anchors so we can get per-anchor recall?

3) Compliance/data flow — I looped in our security team. We need clarity on audit logs (who can see tokens/requests) and whether the pilot can run on Dedicated or Private infra for PII.

We can provision 250 protected docs into your secure upload for an initial run. Also attaching a small sample doc (sample_protocol_for_eval.docx) that shows the complexity (tables + footnotes + cross-references).

Aisha
Aisha Patel
CTO | Clarion Therapeutics

Subject: Re: Call recap: Long-document workflows & evaluation next steps

Aisha — thanks for the quick turn. Short answers, then concrete next steps and timeline.

1) Example failure case: we exported a single example where the single-pass summarizer omitted a cross-referenced dosing table; the file is in the Drive (tab "failure_cases" in benchmarks_v3.xlsx). We'll also add an anonymized before/after PDF to the Drive for your reviewers.
2) Anchor-based eval: yes — our harness supports anchor tagging. If you provide anchor ids (or we annotate them together), the report will include per-anchor recall and per-anchor hallucination flags.
3) Compliance: pilot options
   - Hosted (fastest): redwood-hosted with encrypted logs and strict retention (suitable for non-PII).
   - Dedicated: reserved capacity in Redwood cloud for Clarion with per-tenant audit logs (recommended for PII).
   - Private: VPC/on-prem package if you require full network isolation (we can scope this; longer lead time).

Pilot proposal & timeline (2–4 weeks):
- Week 0: Confirm sample set (Clarion uploads 250 protected docs to secure upload).
- Week 1: Run the three-model benchmark + targeted table-preservation prompt variants; deliver results and failure-case artifacts.
- Week 2: Joint review and refine prompt set + route configs; select model for pilot.
- Week 3–4: Pilot deployment and SLA tuning on Dedicated capacity (if selected).

Pricing note: pilot estimate attached in mutual_action_plan_clarion.docx. If we need to fast-track Dedicated for SOC2 controls, we can discuss a temporary credits arrangement — Rishi, can you confirm internal approval for a pilot credit up to $10k?

If that looks good I'll schedule a 30-min kickoff for next Tue (Aug 18) to lock sample access and SSO details.

Thanks — looking forward.

Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
